title: Withdraw the named drawout relay's plug-in unit
instruction: Take out the plug-in unit of the relay labelled FEEDER 2 (the label with the yellow marker): lift its handle up to release the latch, pull the unit out of its case by the handle with one hand while the other hand goes under the body to carry its weight, and set it down on the black mat in front of it. Do not touch the other relay, and do not reach into the empty case.
context: Protection relays in substation and switchgear panels are drawout units: to test or replace one, a technician lifts its handle to release the latch, slides the 2 kg electronics unit out of its case while taking its weight, and sets it down. Pulling the wrong relay out removes protection from a circuit that is still in service, and the empty case's rear terminals can still carry current-transformer and supply circuits, so hands stay out of it (the manufacturer's manual warns not to touch the inside of the case).
setup: Positions are from the arm bases (x: cm in front of the line joining the two bases, which are 61 cm apart; y: cm left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot; heights above the table top). Panel: a light-grey 3 mm steel plate standing upright on the table and fixed to it, its front face 38.0 cm in front of the bases, from 12 cm right to 42 cm left of the midline, 34 cm tall, with two cut-outs 16.55 cm wide and 16.15 cm tall. Behind each cut-out is the case of an ABB Relion 615 series relay (REF615 class, flush mounting): a steel box 16.4 cm wide, 16.0 cm tall and 15.3 cm deep behind the panel, its floor 6.5 cm above the table, resting on a stand. The relays are centred 8 cm left of the midline (FEEDER 2) and 30 cm left of the midline (FEEDER 1, in front of the left arm). In each case sits the relay's plug-in unit (2.1 kg, the published weight of the unit alone): a light-grey front frame 17.7 cm square and 2.4 cm thick (front face 35.6 cm in front of the bases, bottom edge 5.3 cm above the table) with the HMI (display, LEDs, keys) on it, and a steel body 15.5 cm wide, 15.1 cm tall and 14.7 cm deep inside the case. The unit is held by its bail handle: a U-shaped bar pivoted on both sides of the frame 5 cm below its top edge, whose 12 mm round cross-bar lies across the bottom of the front at rest (its centre 4.2 cm in front of the panel, 5.8 cm above the table) and stands straight out when the handle is lifted 90 degrees. With the handle down the unit is latched (a pull on the unit moves it at most 5 mm); lifting the handle to 90 degrees releases the latch and cams the unit about 7 mm out, which separates its rear connectors; after that nothing holds it in the case. Labels: each relay has an engraved two-layer laminate label (16 x 4 cm, white face, black letters) centred on the panel 0.8 cm above its frame: 'FEEDER 2 / 52-F2 REF615' with a 3.4 cm yellow dot sticker at its right end, and 'FEEDER 1 / 52-F1 REF615' with a blue dot. Mat: a black rubber mat in two strips, each 15 cm wide (centred 8 cm left of the midline), top 4.5 cm above the table (2 cm below the case floor), on blocks: the front strip from 21.3 to 23.2 cm and the back strip from 31.2 to 35.4 cm in front of the bases, leaving an 8 cm gap for fingers under a unit set across them. The relays are unpowered and their cases unwired; there are no lamps or indicators to reproduce. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The score is the highest level reached. 0.25: the FEEDER 2 handle is lifted more than 45 degrees. 0.5: with the handle past 60 degrees, the unit has come 6 mm or more out of its case (its connectors are parted). 0.75: the unit is wholly out of its case (its back face at least 3 mm in front of the panel) and has not been dropped. 1.0: the unit rests on the mat upright (tilted less than 8 degrees, its bottom within 0.4 cm below to 1 cm above the mat's top), wholly out of the case, and after both grippers have been at least 1.5 cm from it for 2 s a reviewer hooks a spring scale on the FEEDER 1 unit's frame and pulls straight out with 30 N for 1.5 s: it must move less than 5.8 mm (its latch play) and its handle must stay down; otherwise the score stays at 0.75. Score 0 if at any time before that check: the FEEDER 1 handle is lifted more than 15 degrees or the FEEDER 1 unit moves more than 3 mm; a finger touches the FEEDER 1 relay's front frame or handle (in the simulator: comes within 6 mm of them); a finger goes inside the FEEDER 2 case's opening; or the FEEDER 2 unit is dropped (tilted more than 35 degrees, or a bottom corner 2 cm or more below the mat's top). Angles are read from a side photo with a protractor template; distances with a ruler against the panel.
reset_notes: Lift the FEEDER 2 unit off the mat with both hands, slide it back into its case with the handle lifted, push it home and turn the handle down to draw it in and latch it (as in the manufacturer's re-insertion procedure). Check that both handles are down and both units are latched (a light pull does not move them more than 5 mm). About 1 minute.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Published (ABB 615 manual): frame, case, 2.1 kg unit, procedure. Inferred: body clearances, handle, friction. Latch and eject cam are our own geometry; connector retention is a rule (10-30 N). Box colliders; no power (empty case is a no-finger rule). Labels legible only in wrist cameras. Demo carries full mass; robot cam lift reaches 4.5 of 7 mm; 30 N pull in sim after recording. Details in README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (neither handle lifted; around 60 s its left gripper reached to the front of the other relay, FEEDER 1); demo: 1.0
